description: The Canada1Water team released a gridded hydraulic-property map for the upper zero-to-fifty-centimetre soil layer across continental Canada and watersheds shared with the United States. The article describes mineral-soil inputs drawn from 250-metre OpenLandMap maps, depth aggregation, and Rosetta v3 pedotransfer estimates of water retention and saturated hydraulic conductivity. It also describes classes for exposed bedrock and peat. Zenodo lists 57 ten-degree GeoTIFF macrotiles plus styles, overview and documentation files in this public CC BY 4.0 release. The 18-band raster encodes soil classes and source or derived hydraulic attributes. Coverage is national-scale model input, not field-measured hydraulic conductivities at every pixel. OpenLandMap uncertainty, pedotransfer assumptions and class assignments are known limitations for local infiltration estimates; the article also notes special handling of small offshore islands in the model domain. A reviewer-assessed use is setting upper-layer infiltration parameters in coupled groundwater and surface-water simulations. model-wflow and data-isric-soilgrids-global-soil-maps are related modelling and soil-map resources, without verified direct compatibility. The separate fifty-to-one-hundred-centimetre layer has its own Zenodo DOI. No raster or archive was downloaded.
